text:
Tara: heads up — CI eval-runner failed on master after the tokenizer PR landed. bscore unit tests started failing with tiny norm diffs, looks like a numeric/aggregation edge.
ci-bot: [CI] eval-runner #4223 failed: test_bertscore_norms (tests/test_metrics.py::TestBERTScore)
Mike: can you paste the failing snippet from the job logs?
Tara: sure, here are the relevant lines from the runner output:
```
E   AssertionError: |norm(ref) - norm(pred)| = 3.2e-06 >= 1e-06
E   assert abs(0.9999987 - 0.9999955) < 1e-06
```
Ana: hmm that amount of drift smells like a tokenization change that altered per-token embedding counts, then the pooling/normalization strategy didn't compensate. we recently switched to the new subword splitter that emits different special-token handling.
Sam: to add context — our BERTScore impl normalizes token embeddings *before* mean pooling, then trusts the pooled vector's norm ~1. if token counts change, the pooled norm can slightly deviate. quantization (int8) and mixed-precision CI runs make it borderline.
Rachel: pass@k/exactmatch tests are clean, so not a dataset ingestion bug. this is specifically in embedding aggregation for BERTScore and how we assert the final norm close to 1.
Lee: quick repro I ran locally: the difference is reproducible when you run with the new tokenizer + small random seed. patch below fixes by explicitly re-normalizing the pooled vector after averaging.
```
# fix: re-normalize pooled embedding after mean
pooled = embeddings.mean(dim=1)
pooled = pooled / (pooled.norm(p=2, dim=-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-12)
```
Ana: that seems correct. originally we assumed mean of unit vectors ~ unit length; that's not guaranteed with variable token counts or quantization noise.
Tara: ok — what's the plan? do we patch and then re-run historical snapshots? or relax the assertion threshold?
Sam: prefer patch + targeted re-eval. relaxing threshold hides real regressions. we should re-run the BERTScore smoke suite on the last 30 model snapshots (fast sample) to ensure no behavioral changes.
Mike: also add a unit test that simulates different tokenization slices and checks pooled norm == 1 after the norm step, and CI should run that in float32 and quantized modes.
Rachel: also note: dashboard aggregation in console currently stores raw pooled vectors for a couple of old snapshots. after fix we should backfill normalized vectors or mark them as pre-normalization in the metadata to avoid confusing historical comparisons.
Lee: I'll open a PR with the code tweak + unit test. will also add a small test harness to run quantized runner (int8) locally in CI for this test. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-runner/pull/891 (WIP)
Tara: can someone create a short ticket for re-eval/backfill and add to the weekly eng-ml board? put it as high priority for model-onboarding flows; we don't want onboarding blocked by metric noise.
Ana: created ticket INF-7342 and added checklist: run smoke on last 30 snapshots, run full eval on any snapshots where delta > 1e-4, backfill dashboard metadata, add release note.
Mike: assign me to the dashboard backfill piece.
Tara: thanks — assigning reviewers @Ana @Lee. I'll kick off the smoke re-eval after PR merge and ping the CI job. :thumbsup:
